input.title: From islamic warriors to drug lords: The evolution of the taliban insurgency
input.abstract: Farhana Schmidt focuses on the evolution of the Taliban insurgency and Afghanistan being at the epicenter of conflict. The resulting drug production labs and drug trafficking have produced an economic miracle in a land that is, without doubt, one of the world's most remote and backward regions. A lack of confidence and trust in the Afghan government also gives opium an added value. The answer lies in the lessons the Taliban have learned from their predecessors, the mujahideen. The mujahideen exacted payments from local farmers through taxation in the 1980s, and tolls from traders at checkpoints marked carefully along key routes. Afghanistan has been without a functional central bank, treasury, tax collection system, customs control, civil service, and judicial system for more than a quarter of a century. Its cash economy has allowed the Taliban to step in and run roughshod over this state to the point that it is barely recognizable as one.
